government.title: Government put Rs 800.7 crore into Asian Games preparation
government.summary: New figures show the sports ministry spent Rs 702.9 crore through its Annual Competition and Training Calendar and Rs 97.8 crore via TOPS on the 501-athlete Aichi-Nagoya contingent, with the single biggest slice (Rs 251.4 crore) going to international exposure trips. TOPS chief N.S. Johal said the squad, 310 of them first-time Asiad competitors and 65 from Khelo India, has momentum to match or better India's 106-medal Hangzhou 2022 haul.

markets.title: Kabaddi Champions League doubles down with two more franchises
markets.summary: The KCL is expanding to a 10-team format for season two, adding Jind Jaguars and Kurukshetra Knights. Chairman Balwan Singh pitched the league as a genuine talent pipeline rather than a cricket-style exhibition, noting nine of the 12 players who made India's most recent Asiad kabaddi squads came through it, a concrete claim for a non-cricket league trying to prove its business case.

society.title: Para-shooters deliver a landmark team gold in Changwon
society.summary: Millie Shah, Mona Agarwal and Avani Lekhara won team gold at the World Shooting Para Sport World Championships, with Shah and Rakesh Nidagundi also taking individual medals, a strong result for India's Paralympic pipeline that arrived with none of the fanfare around the Asian Games this week, despite Lekhara being a two-time Paralympic gold medallist.

society.title: Women's cricket, not the men's team, headlines India's Asiad day
society.summary: With the Aichi-Nagoya opening ceremony still a day away, India's marquee fixture today is the women's cricket team's quarter-final against hosts Japan under Harmanpreet Kaur, alongside a 3-0 soft-tennis win over Laos and teqball debutant Quimcy D'Souza upsetting Japan's top seed to reach the semi-final in a sport making its Asian Games debut.

society.title: India's chess Olympiad defence survives a hotel row and a rating dip
society.summary: The title defence in Samarkand opened with Indian GMs Srinath Narayanan and Vidit Gujrathi publicly complaining their team waited five-plus hours with no rooms assigned; FIDE responded by compensating affected teams. On the board, India beat Thailand and Indonesia in the first two rounds, though Gukesh's live rating dropped below 2700 for the first time in four years after a round-two draw.

government.title: US Senate advances the Protect College Sports Act
government.summary: The bill, a one-time no-penalty transfer rule, a limited antitrust exemption letting schools pool media rights, and the first federal NIL rules, cleared a Senate procedural hurdle with a floor vote expected next week, though the House is in recess until October and the clock runs out when this Congress ends. Nick Saban criticised college sport's drift from development to focusing on money; Senator Jeff Merkley opposed the bill for curbing athletes' bargaining power.

government.title: Russian athletes take World Athletics ban fight to the IOC and UN
government.summary: Russian athletes wrote to the IOC and the UN Human Rights Commissioner calling World Athletics' ongoing ban collective punishment, pointing out that the IOC, FIBA and FIA have all moved toward reinstating Russians and Belarusians under neutral status since the 2022 suspension. World Athletics reaffirmed its ban in July; Russian Athletics has since filed two appeals to the Court of Arbitration for Sport.

markets.title: NBA owners weigh $10bn-plus expansion into Las Vegas and Seattle
markets.summary: The Board of Governors discussed expansion bids reportedly around $10 billion per franchise for the two markets, a sharp jump on recent expansion pricing. No vote has been scheduled and the league stresses nothing is decided, but the number alone resets expectations for what a new NBA franchise costs.

markets.title: PGA Tour shuts the door on a LIV return as bankruptcy fallout deepens
markets.summary: Tour CEO Brian Rolapp said the Tour is not currently contemplating a returning member programme for LIV defectors. That lands as LIV Golf works through Chapter 11 (filed September 8, $500m-$1bn in liabilities) after Saudi Arabia's PIF, which had put in over $5bn since 2022, stopped funding it; events and prize money have already been cut. The Tour is meanwhile finalising a two-tier restructure for 2028 with expanded DP World Tour co-events.

markets.title: PWHL lands its first full-season national US broadcast deal
markets.summary: The Professional Women's Hockey League signed with Scripps Sports for 2026-27: a Saturday Game of the Week on ION, reaching 128 million-plus households, plus two more national games a week on Scripps' free streaming network and the Walter Cup Finals on ION. It lands as the league expands to 12 teams, adding Detroit and Las Vegas.

markets.title: Five major leagues push regulators for a cross-state bettor blocklist
markets.summary: MLB, MLS, the NBA, NFL and NHL, with their players' associations, formally petitioned state gambling regulators for permanent bans on bettors who threaten athletes or their families, a standardised cross-operator reporting system, and licensing terms that force sportsbooks to flag abusive accounts proactively.

society.title: Players go public on bettor harassment as gambling ads saturate broadcasts
society.summary: Behind this week's regulatory push sits a starker story: NBA guard Fred VanVleet said players carry all of the burden and danger that comes with the league's association to gambling without ever being consulted, as a gambling logo or ad now appears roughly every 13 seconds on US sports TV. The proximate trigger was MLB pitcher Lance McCullers Jr. hiring 24-hour security after a bettor threatened his five-year-old daughter over a bad outing.

opportunities.title: What Rs 800 crore actually buys: a cost-per-medal model for India's Asiad campaign
opportunities.summary: The spending breakdown by scheme (ACTC vs TOPS) is public, and so is Hangzhou's 106-medal haul. Nobody has built the cost-per-medal comparison across cycles to test whether the funding increase is translating into proportionate returns.

opportunities.title: LIV Golf's bankruptcy is the real verdict on sportswashing's shelf life
opportunities.summary: PIF's exit and the Chapter 11 filing are being covered as a golf business story. The bigger, unmade argument is about whether sovereign-wealth sports investment has a natural expiry once the geopolitical utility fades, with LIV as the first hard data point.

opportunities.title: Can a bettor ban in Ohio actually stop him betting in Nevada?
opportunities.summary: The leagues' joint letter got clean pickup as a headline. The unanswered, more interesting question is the plumbing: US sports betting is regulated state by state, and nobody has explained on record whether a cross-operator blocklist is technically enforceable at all.

opportunities.title: Two kabaddi leagues, one market: does Indian kabaddi have room for KCL and PKL both
opportunities.summary: KCL's expansion to 10 teams is being reported as a straight growth story. The franchise-economics question of whether a single-sport market the size of Indian kabaddi can sustain two competing leagues long-term hasn't been asked directly anywhere.

opportunities.title: FIDE's Samarkand hotel failure is an infrastructure signal, not a one-off
opportunities.summary: The accommodation row made news as an embarrassing anecdote about India's team waiting five hours for rooms. Read against a broader pattern, it's a live case study in whether federations are over-committing prestige events to markets that can't yet host them at scale.

opportunities.title: India's women cricketers, not the men, are the face of this Asian Games, and why that's new
opportunities.summary: Women's cricket business coverage usually means WPL valuations. This is a different and fresher angle: a multi-sport Games where the women's team, not the men's, is the marquee national fixture, and what that visibility parity is actually worth.
